confirmed.problem: The speak loop used to run on Dispatchers.Default. It now runs on the controller's Main scope, so tts.speak() runs on the UI thread. AutomaticTTSService.speak calls packInstalled() and kokoro.ensureReady(). On the first utterance, ensureReady() → initEngine() loads the Kokoro ONNX model (model.int8.onnx, voices.bin, espeak data) on Main. That risks an ANR or a long freeze, and the file checks run on Main before every paragraph.
confirmed.evidence: ReaderSpeechController.kt:48 `private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + Job())`; :251 `currentSpeakJob = scope.launch {` (was `scope.launch(Dispatchers.Default) {`); :269 `tts.speak(text)`; AutomaticTTSService.kt:58 `val engine = if (packInstalled() && kokoro.ensureReady()) kokoro else device`; KokoroTTSController.kt `if (tts == null) initEngine()`

verdict.why:
Confirmed, but the risk is narrower than the reviewer says. The patch does move the speak loop onto Main: ReaderSpeechController.kt:48 makes the scope Dispatchers.Main, and speakCurrent now uses `scope.launch {` where it used `scope.launch(Dispatchers.Default)`. AutomaticTTSService.speak (line 58) then calls packInstalled() and kokoro.ensureReady() on Main. Neither function is wrapped in withContext.

What the reviewer overstates: the model is usually not loaded on the first utterance. KokoroTTSController has `init { initEngine() }`, so when the pack is already installed, OfflineTts loads in the constructor. That constructor runs on Main through `remember { ReaderSpeechController(context) }` in ReaderScreen.kt:267. This happened before the patch too, so it is not a new regression. Once tts is set, or failedToOpen is set, ensureReady() does not load the model again.

What is new: when the pack is missing at construction and downloaded later, the first speak() calls initEngine() → OfflineTts(...) on the UI thread. Before the patch this ran on Default. The reader steers users into this path: it offers the Kokoro download when the status is MODEL_NOT_DOWNLOADED. Expect a multi-second freeze, with an ANR possible.

Minor: packInstalled() → TTSDownloadWorker.isModelDownloaded makes about six File.exists()/length() calls on Main before each paragraph. That is a StrictMode disk-read cost, not an ANR.

Not a problem: Kokoro synthesis and AudioTrack writes run in Kokoro's own Dispatchers.Default scope, and speak only join()s, which suspends rather than blocks.

Smallest fix: wrap the call in `withContext(Dispatchers.Default)`, either around tts.speak in the loop or inside AutomaticTTSService.speak around the ensureReady/packInstalled pick.

confirmed.problem: Tapping Next or Previous (or the MediaSession skip) while a paragraph is being pulled loses a paragraph. A pull is slowest at a resource boundary, where Readium loads the next HTML file. speakCurrent() cancels the job doing the pull. The source has already advanced the Readium iterator and taken chunks.next() inside withContext(IO), and the cancelled withContext throws that text away. The paragraph is never queued. After Next, the loop then pulls twice to reach the bumped index, so the queue is out of step and P_N and P_N+1 are both skipped. After Previous, P_N is never read. beginSeeking avoids cancelling for exactly this reason, but skipForward/skipBackward still cancel.
confirmed.evidence: ReaderSpeechController.kt:192-199 `currentIndex++\n        speakCurrent()`; :246 `currentSpeakJob?.cancel()`; :205 `// Let an in-flight paragraph pull finish so seeking cannot drop its text.`; ReaderContentText.kt:38 `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {` … :42 `val element = iterator?.nextOrNull()` … :51 `chunks.next()`

verdict.why:
I confirmed this by reading the code. It is a regression introduced by this patch: before it, `currentQueue` was a complete list that `paragraphs()` had already loaded.

The failure path:
- While playing, the loop in `speakCurrent()` (ReaderSpeechController.kt:253-261) runs `currentIndex++` after each paragraph and then calls `nextParagraph()`, which runs `source.next()` with `currentIndex == currentQueue.size`.
- `skipForward()` and `skipBackward()` (:192-199) call `speakCurrent()`, and its first line is `currentSpeakJob?.cancel()` (:246). Nothing there checks `pullingParagraph`; only `pause()` (:278) and `beginSeeking()` (:205) avoid cancelling a pull.
- In ReaderContentText.kt:38-52 the source changes its state inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`. `iterator.nextOrNull()` advances the Readium iterator, and `chunks.next()` takes a chunk out of `chunks`. Kotlin's `withContext` has a prompt-cancellation guarantee: if the caller is cancelled while the block runs, the block's result is thrown away and `CancellationException` is raised, even when the block finished. Because the text was already taken from the iterator, that paragraph is lost for good.
- `nextParagraph()` (:236) re-throws the cancellation, so line 261 never adds the paragraph to the queue.

What the user hears:
- **After Next:** `currentIndex` is N+1 and the queue size is N. The new loop pulls twice. P_{N+1} goes into slot N and P_{N+2} into slot N+1, so P_{N+2} is spoken. Both P_N and P_{N+1} are skipped, and every later queue index points one paragraph too far.
- **After Previous:** P_{N-1} is replayed, then the index goes to N and the next pull returns P_{N+1}. P_N is never read.

A pull at a resource boundary, where Readium loads the next HTML file, makes the window wider, but the bug can happen on any pull.

Nothing in the code refutes this. The `pullingParagraph` flag exists, but `speakCurrent()` and the skip functions never check it.

confirmed.problem: Android writes its own converterVersion (1) into the same iOS-named sidecar that backup and sync carry, and iOS reads that file. iOS ignores converterPlatform and compares the number against its converter version, which is 9. So every work Android imports or rebuilds shows as stale on iOS (rebuild pill, 'Kudos has a newer way…', staleWorks). Every record iOS writes, and every record from before this patch, has no platform field, so Android always treats it as stale. On Android that means immediate rebuild without confirmation in My copy and a permanent reader pill. The two apps keep marking each other's output stale, and Android's rebuild replaces the iOS record in the shared folder.
confirmed.evidence: WorkConversionRecord.kt:20 `val isStale: Boolean get() = converterPlatform != "android" || converterVersion < CURRENT_VERSION`; :26 `const val CURRENT_VERSION = 1`; WorkImporter.kt:368 `converterPlatform = "android"`; SyncRepository.kt:346-350 exports it as `BackupPaths.iosConversionRecordFileName(work.id)`; iOS ImportedDocumentConverter.swift:46 `static let converterVersion = 9`; iOS WorkConversionRecord.swift `converterVersion < ImportedDocumentConverter.converterVersion`

verdict.why:
I confirmed the core claim by reading the code, with one part overstated.

What holds:
- **Android now writes its own records.** WorkConversionRecord.kt sets `CURRENT_VERSION = 1`. WorkImporter.recordConversion writes `converterPlatform="android"` both after an import that isn't EPUB and after `rebuildFromOriginal`. It writes to the same `<id>.conversion.json` that BackupRepository:157-158 and SyncRepository:346-347 export under `iosConversionRecordFileName`.
- **iOS ignores the platform field.** iOS WorkConversionRecord.swift is `converterVersion < ImportedDocumentConverter.converterVersion`, and `converterVersion = 9` (ImportedDocumentConverter.swift:46). It has no `converterPlatform` property, and JSONDecoder drops unknown keys. KudosBackup.swift:3350-3359 restores `.conversion.json` files from the archive or sync folder to `WorkConversionRecord.url` when the device has none. So a v1 Android stamp reads as stale on iOS (`WorkReconversion.candidate`/`staleWorks`, the reader pill, and the rebuild section in WorkProvenanceSections).
- **Android treats every iOS record as stale.** `isStale` is `converterPlatform != "android" || ...`, and iOS never writes that field. Android's own test asserts that a v999 iOS record is stale. That drives the reader rebuild entry, the "Kudos has a newer way…" copy in My copy, and the RebuildOriginalDialog `LaunchedEffect`, which rebuilds right away with no confirmation when the work is stale. Before this patch Android always asked first.
- **An Android rebuild replaces iOS's v9 stamp.** It overwrites the record with Android's v1 stamp, and backup and sync then export that. An iOS restore onto a device without that record gets a stale record where a current one used to be. The two apps mark each other's output stale in both directions.

What is overstated: works Android imported were already stale on iOS before this patch. Android wrote no record, and iOS treats a missing record as v0. So the iOS side of the Android-import case is not a new regression. Two things are new: iOS stamps get overwritten, and Android flags every iOS-converted work as stale and rebuilds it without confirmation.

confirmed.problem: Hold-seek differs from iOS, which is the source of truth. iOS steps through the book's positions, moves the reader there (book.go), and re-anchors speech at the new locator on release. Android only moves an index in its own speech queue and shows a text preview; the page never moves. The queue begins at the locator where reading started, so holding Previous stops at that paragraph and cannot seek back into earlier text, which iOS can.
confirmed.evidence: ReaderSpeechController.kt:220 `val target = ReaderSpeechSeek.seekIndex(currentIndex, currentQueue.size, delta) ?: return@launch` / `seekPreview.value = currentQueue[target]`; iOS ReadiumReaderView.swift:1738-1745 `ReaderSpeechSkip.seekIndex(current: currentIdx, count: positions.count…` → `book.go(to: locator)`; `speech.reanchor(to: book.currentLocator, resumePlaying: speechSeekWasPlaying)`

verdict.why: Confirmed. In the patch, ReaderSpeechController.seek (lines ~212-224) only changes currentIndex inside its own currentQueue and sets seekPreview, which feeds spokenText. Nothing calls the navigator. onUtteranceStart is never assigned outside the controller, and the only seek callbacks in ReaderScreen.kt (lines 742-745: onSeekSpeech, onSpeechSeekStart, onSpeechSeekEnd) go to the controller. So the page never moves during a hold-seek. startReading (ReaderScreen.kt:727) builds the queue from ReaderContentText.source(publication, from = the live locator), and startReading clears the queue and sets currentIndex to 0. ReaderSpeechSeek.seekIndex(currentIndex, currentQueue.size, -1) therefore cannot go below the paragraph where reading started, so holding Previous cannot reach earlier text. iOS handleSpeechSeekHoldTick (ReadiumReaderView.swift ~1714-1745) instead steps through book.currentChapterPositions, calls book.go(to: locator) and noteSeekLocator. On release, handleSpeechSeekHoldEnd calls speech.reanchor(to: book.currentLocator, resumePlaying:), so iOS moves the page and can seek back before the start point. Two smaller differences: Android seeks in paragraph steps, while iOS uses Readium positions limited to the current chapter, and endSeeking resumes from the queue index without re-anchoring to a page.

confirmed.problem: initEngine became an expression-bodied function with no declared return type, but its lambda body still uses bare `return` (lines 78 and the model-missing branch). Kotlin (2.3.21 here) rejects `return` in an expression body whose return type is inferred, so this file probably does not compile. This is unfinished work from the agent's last edit. The fix is a block body (`private fun initEngine() { synchronized(engineLock) { ... } }`) or labelled `return@synchronized`.

verdict.why:
I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not compile it, because the task is read-only and there is no kotlinc on this machine.

In the uncommitted diff in /Users/cidy02/kudos-agent-codex, android/app/src/main/java/io/github/cidy02/kudos/reader/speech/KokoroTTSController.kt line 77 changed from a block body, `private fun initEngine() {`, to an expression body, `private fun initEngine() = synchronized(engineLock) {`, with no declared return type. The lambda still contains bare `return` in two places: the new guard `if (tts != null || disposed || failedToOpen) return` and the existing model-missing branch (`_status.value = SpeechStatus.UNAVAILABLE` followed by `return`). Because synchronized is inline, those are non-local returns from initEngine, so the function has an expression body, an inferred return type and returns inside it.

The cached Kotlin 2.3.21 compiler jar (kotlin-compiler-embeddable-2.3.21.jar) contains the diagnostic text "Returns are prohibited in functions with expression body and without explicit return type. Use block body '{...}' or add an explicit return type." Its LanguageFeature class has AllowReturnInExpressionBodyWithExplicitType, which means returns are allowed only when the type is declared. The Gradle files set no languageVersion or apiVersion override.

So the file should fail to compile. Fix: use a block body, `private fun initEngine() { synchronized(engineLock) { ... } }`, or declare `: Unit`.

confirmed.problem: Sync reverts local edits and deletions. The digest Android remembers is null whenever sync leaves anything outstanding (`settled` false: an EPUB is pending or missing). The next sync then treats Android's own previous manifest as foreign: importManifest → importPackage → restorePronunciations merges it with archive-wins. So a correction the user edited after the last sync is overwritten with the old value, and a deleted one comes back. The new `nativeManifestDigest` is always written, but it is only checked inside the `ownManifest` branch. iOS skips its own last manifest, so it does not behave this way.
confirmed.evidence: line 230 `if (ownManifest) {` … line 243 `val outcome = importManifest(syncDir, manifest)`; line 411 `if (settled) BackupPaths.sha256(manifestBytes) else null`; BackupRepository.kt:417 `pronunciationStore.apply(merge.sourceManifest.pronunciations)` (merging = `global + incoming.global`, incoming wins)

verdict.why: I confirmed the mechanism by reading the code. I could not refute it. In SyncRepository.kt, line 411 stores `lastManifestDigest` as null whenever `settled` is false. That happens when `folderViewIsCurrent` is false, when any work has `remoteEpubPending`, or when a work has `hasEpub` but its local file is missing. With the digest null, `ownManifest` at line 228 is false on the next sync, so Android's own previous manifest goes to `importManifest` at line 243. That calls `backupRepository.importPackage`, which reaches `restorePronunciations` and then `pronunciationStore.apply(merge.sourceManifest.pronunciations)`. `PronunciationCorrections.merging` is `global + incoming.global`, and the per-layer merges work the same way: incoming wins and the result is a union. The import runs before the export. So if the user changes a correction's IPA after the last sync, the old value comes back. If the user deletes a word, the word comes back. The new `nativeManifestDigest` is written on every sync, but it is only checked inside the `ownManifest` branch, so it does not prevent this. Other record types use clock-based merges (concurrentRowsDeferred), but pronunciations have no clock, so they are the ones exposed. One correction to the claim: iOS also withholds its stamp while `pendingRemoteAssetsKey` is set (FolderSyncService.swift:313-316 and 385-391), and in that case it re-restores its own manifest too. So iOS does not always skip its own last manifest. Android's unsettled condition is broader, though: it also covers a missing local EPUB and an unfolded conflict copy. The patch therefore causes real reverts and resurrections of local pronunciation edits on Android.

confirmed.problem: captureLibrarySnapshot calls pronunciationStore.load() with nothing to catch an error. load() throws on a malformed or undecodable kokoro-pronunciations.json. Every export, every import (import also calls captureLibrarySnapshot for `current`) and every sync run therefore fails because of one bad corrections file. iOS `KudosBackupPronunciations.capture` uses a load() that never throws and treats a missing or bad file as empty (KokoroPronunciationStore.swift load()). The restore side catches this (restorePronunciations); the capture side does not.
confirmed.evidence: `pronunciations = pronunciationStore.load().corrections(),` with KokoroPronunciationStore.kt:48 `if (file.exists()) json.decodeFromString<Document>(file.readText()) else Document()` (throws SerializationException)

verdict.why: Confirmed. In the patched BackupRepository.kt:330, captureLibrarySnapshot calls `pronunciationStore.load().corrections()` with nothing around it to catch an error. KokoroPronunciationStore.kt:46-49 load() decodes with `json.decodeFromString<Document>(file.readText())` whenever the file exists. That throws a SerializationException on a malformed or undecodable file, or an IOException if the file can't be read. On purpose, the store has no fallback: its comment says a malformed file must not turn into an empty one. captureLibrarySnapshot is called by export (line 59), by both import paths for `current` (lines 107 and 121), by the path at line 295, and by sync (SyncRepository.kt:278). So one bad kokoro-pronunciations.json makes every one of them fail. ReaderScreen.kt:475 does wrap its own load() in runCatching, so other callers do guard it; capture does not. iOS KokoroPronunciationStore.load() (in kudos-ios-polish) uses `try?` and falls back, so it never throws, and backup capture there treats a bad file as having no corrections. That is a regression against iOS, which is the source of truth. The fix: in capture, use `runCatching { pronunciationStore.load().corrections() }.getOrDefault(PronunciationCorrections())`. The store's no-fallback behaviour should stay for the edit paths (apply, setOverride, removeOverride), so that a bad file is never overwritten.

confirmed.problem: The sync path that restores a legacy `Kudos.kudosbackup` ignores the new pronunciationsRestoreFailed flag. If the corrections fail to save there, sync still reports success and goes on to export. That export publishes a manifest without the archive's corrections, so they are lost from the folder. importManifest (line 607) throws on the same failure; this path does not.
confirmed.evidence: `backupRepository.importV2ZipBytes(bytes)` (result discarded) vs line 607 `if (summary.pronunciationsRestoreFailed) { throw IOException("Could not save pronunciation corrections. ...") }`

verdict.why:
Confirmed. In SyncRepository.kt:263-268, the legacy branch calls `backupRepository.importV2ZipBytes(bytes)` and throws the result away. That import goes through applyMergeResultLocked, then restorePronunciations (BackupRepository.kt ~386/417). restorePronunciations catches the store failure and returns `pronunciationsRestoreFailed = true` instead of throwing. Nothing checks that flag on this path, so sync goes on to step 2 and exports.

The exported manifest's pronunciations come from `pronunciationStore.load()` in captureLibrarySnapshot, so they do not include the archive's corrections. carryUnknownRecordKeys cannot recover them either: this branch runs only when the folder has no Kudos.json manifest, so there is no replaced manifest to carry from.

importManifest (line 607) checks the same flag and throws, which keeps the folder intact; this path does not. That breaks the invariant that a restore never loses data either app keeps.

One correction to the claim: the corrections are not deleted from the folder. Kudos.kudosbackup is never deleted (its only reference is line 263). But once a Kudos.json manifest exists, later syncs take the manifest branch and never read the legacy archive again. The corrections are therefore missing from the published manifest and never retried.

confirmed.problem: Browse's filter badge now disagrees with Browse's own hero, which is the mismatch row #99 was meant to remove. `activeFilterCount` now leaves out `filters.searchSubject().text`. Browse's filters do not carry the fandom, so when only one tag field is set (for example one character), that character becomes the 'subject' and is not counted. The Browse hero leaves out only `fandomName`, so it still counts that character. Example: on Naruto, add the character Sasuke. The hero's Filters cell shows 1, but the button shows no number: the badge only appears when `narrowed` is true, and its count is now 0.
confirmed.evidence: FandomWorksScreen.kt:114 `val activeFilters = remember(filters) { activeFilterCount(filters) }` and :161 `badgeCount = if (narrowed) activeFilters else 0`, against :271 `filterLabels = summaryLabels(filters, excluding = fandomName)`. New SearchFilterHelpers.kt:131 `summaryLabels(filters, excluding = filters.searchSubject().text, includesSort = false).size`. SearchLocalMatches.kt:128-130 makes a single filled tag field the subject.

verdict.why: I confirmed the finding by reading the code; nothing was built or run. In FandomWorksScreen.kt, line 114 sets the badge from `activeFilterCount(filters)`, and line 161 shows it only when `narrowed` is true. In the patch, `activeFilterCount` (SearchFilterHelpers.kt:130-131) is `summaryLabels(filters, excluding = filters.searchSubject().text, includesSort = false).size`. Browse starts from `browseBaseline()`, which is `AO3SearchFilters(sort = DATE_UPDATED)` with no fandom (AO3BrowseRepository.kt:173-174). So adding the single character Sasuke leaves `characters = "Sasuke"` as the only filled tag field. `searchSubject()` (SearchLocalMatches.kt:119-133) then returns "Sasuke", and `addTagField` filters out that name, so the badge count is 0. The hero gets `summaryLabels(filters, excluding = fandomName)` (FandomWorksScreen.kt:271), and SearchResultsHero.kt:234 counts every non-Sort label, so its Filters cell counts Sasuke as 1. The badge and the hero disagree. The patch makes Search consistent, where the hero's subject is `searchSubject()`, but it breaks Browse, where the subject is `fandomName`. The same mismatch occurs with a single relationship, a single freeform tag, or a single warning on its own.

confirmed.problem: The patch changed the test helper that stands in for a real browser so it now follows the app's new rule, and that rule differs from both a browser and iOS. The helper is documented as an independent browser oracle, and the existing whole-form comparisons at :61 and :124 use it. Now it drops an enabled hidden "0" whenever its checkbox is disabled or ticked. A browser sends both values. iOS (`submittedHiddenFields`) drops a hidden field only when the hidden input itself is disabled; for a ticked box it swaps in the box's value. Production makes the same disabled-box divergence: AO3ChallengeSettingsForm.kt:68 skips the hidden "0" when only the box is disabled, where iOS still posts it. The existing tests can no longer catch a divergence from browser or iOS behaviour.
confirmed.evidence: Test helper doc: `/** Independent fixture browser oracle; deliberately does not call the app snapshot/serializer. */`, with the added branch `type == "hidden" && form.selectFirst("input[type=checkbox][name='${element.attr("name")}']")?.let { box -> box.hasAttr("disabled") || box.hasAttr("checked") } == true -> emptyList()`. Production :68 `if (companionBox.disabled || this@AO3ChallengeSettingsForm[served.name] == "1") return@forEachIndexed`. iOS keeps the hidden field unless it is disabled: `for input in … "input[type=hidden][name]" … where enabled(input)`, and only a ticked, enabled box replaces its value.

verdict.why:
Confirmed by reading the code. The patch adds a branch to `browserSubmission` in AO3ChallengeSettingsEditTest.kt (around line 350). That helper is documented as an "Independent fixture browser oracle" and is the expected value in the whole-form comparisons at lines 61 and 124. The new branch drops an enabled hidden input whenever a checkbox with the same name is disabled or ticked. A real browser does not do this: it sends every enabled hidden input, then also sends a ticked box's value. So the oracle now just mirrors the new production rule, and those comparisons can no longer catch a divergence from browser behaviour.

Production also differs from iOS. In AO3ChallengeSettingsForm.kt the new code is `if (companionBox.disabled || ...[served.name] == "1") return@forEachIndexed`. That skips an enabled hidden "0" when only its checkbox is disabled. iOS `submittedHiddenFields` (kudos-ios-polish Services/AO3Client+Challenges.swift:243) works differently:
- It keeps every hidden input that is not itself disabled.
- For a ticked, enabled box, it replaces that hidden field's value with the box's value.

So when the hidden input is enabled but its box is disabled, iOS posts "0" and Android posts nothing.

The ticked-and-enabled case gives the same final value on both platforms, though the field's position in the request may differ. In real Rails `check_box` markup, `disabled` usually lands on both inputs, so the disabled-box mismatch is rare in practice. It is still a real departure from iOS and from a browser, and the weakened oracle hides it.

confirmed.problem: The picker now accepts every file type, but each picked file is still read whole into memory before its format is checked, and the bytes are kept in `pendingImports` until the date-confirmation dialog closes. Before, the picker excluded videos, images and other large binaries. Now a user can pick one (or several at once) and run the app out of memory, only to be told afterwards that the format is unsupported. iOS's `.data` catch-all goes through a lazy file URL rather than a heap copy.
confirmed.evidence: SettingsPages2.kt:95 `internal val EpubOpenMimeTypes = arrayOf("*/*")` → ExternalFileImport.offer → DocumentImportPreparation.kt:38 `context.contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)?.use { it.readBytes() }` with no size cap; the result is stored as `PendingDocumentImport(uri, displayName, bytes, detection)` and accumulated in KudosApp.kt `pendingImports = pendingImports + preparation.imports`.

verdict.why: I confirmed the claim, with one caveat about how it fails. The patch changes SettingsPages2.kt:95 from a 5-type list (epub, pdf, html, plain, octet-stream) to `arrayOf("*/*")`. The SAF picker (OpenMultipleDocuments) therefore now offers videos and images, which it filtered out before. The picked URIs go through ExternalFileImport.offer and KudosApp.kt:185 to prepareDocumentImports. There, DocumentImportPreparation.kt:38 does `openInputStream(uri)?.use { it.readBytes() }` with no size cap, and it does this before any format check, because format detection happens later in WorkImporter. The bytes are kept in `PendingDocumentImport.bytes` and added to `pendingImports` (KudosApp.kt:186) until the confirmation dialog closes. readBytes also needs about 2–3x the file size while its buffer grows. The caveat: runCatching catches Throwable, so a single file too large to allocate may only produce a "failure" entry instead of a crash. But several medium-sized media files (tens to hundreds of MB each) can each read successfully and pile up in pendingImports. That exhausts the heap, and the OOM then hits somewhere that is not caught (UI or importer). The user is only told the format is unsupported after the bytes have already been loaded. DocumentImportPreparation.kt itself is unchanged; this patch is what newly exposes it to arbitrary media. I didn't open the iOS code, so I haven't verified the reviewer's point that iOS's `.data` catch-all uses a lazy file URL, but it doesn't affect whether the Android bug is real. Fix: keep a filtered MIME list, or check size and format before readBytes.

confirmed.problem: With `*/*`, the formats iOS detects and refuses with specific guidance now reach Android's sniffer, which has no case for them. An .rtf is plain printable text, so it is imported as a work full of RTF control words. A .docx or .odt is a ZIP, so the user gets the archive message instead of iOS's Word/OpenDocument guidance. A .mobi gets a generic message. The result notes claim the rejections carry 'iOS's conversion guidance'; for these formats they do not.
confirmed.evidence: ImportedFileFormat.kt:14 `EPUB, PDF, HTML, TEXT, ZIP, UNKNOWN;` and :38 `else -> if (head.isProbablyText()) TEXT else UNKNOWN`; WorkImporter.kt:481-482 `ImportedFileFormat.ZIP -> "Couldn't find anything readable in that archive. It needs an EPUB, " +`. iOS ImportedFileFormat.swift:24-30 adds `case docx`, `case odt`, `case rtf`, `case mobi`, `case rar`, `case sevenZip`, and ImportedDocumentConverter gives "\(format.displayName) import is coming in a later update. For now, convert it to EPUB (calibre, or Word's \"Save as\")…" / "Kindle files aren't supported yet. Convert it to EPUB with calibre…".

verdict.why:
Confirmed by reading the code. The patch changes `EpubOpenMimeTypes` in SettingsPages2.kt:95 from five specific MIME types to `"*/*"`. The sniffer in ImportedFileFormat.kt is unchanged and only knows EPUB, PDF, HTML, TEXT, ZIP and UNKNOWN. Nothing filters by file name before sniffing: `importLocalEpub` at WorkImporter.kt:233 calls `sniff` directly, and `isSupportedFileName` is not used on this path.

- **RTF:** starts with `{\rtf1...`. Braces and backslashes are in the allowed set of `isProbablyText`, so it is classed as TEXT. PlainTextWorkConverter then imports it as a work full of RTF control words.
- **DOCX/ODT:** these are ZIPs without `META-INF/container.xml`, so they are classed as ZIP. ArchiveWorkConverter only picks up .html, .htm, .txt, .md and .xhtml entries (ArchiveWorkConverter.kt:57-58), so it finds nothing and the user gets the "Couldn't find anything readable in that archive" message.
- **MOBI:** binary data, so it is classed as UNKNOWN and gets the new generic "This MOBI file isn't a format Kudos can read" message.

iOS ImportedDocumentConverter.swift:65-72 gives specific guidance instead: for docx/odt/rtf, import is "coming in a later update" with advice to convert to EPUB; for mobi, convert with calibre; rar and 7z have their own case too. The old list already included `application/octet-stream`, so some of these files could get through before. The `*/*` change makes it routine, and RTF files, which used to be filtered out, now get imported as garbage text. That is both a user-visible regression and a mismatch with iOS.

confirmed.problem: The result notes say a picked .kudosbackup 'without readable work entries reports the archive-specific error'. They skip the usual case: a real backup has `works/<uuid>.epub` entries. The picker now lets it through, it sniffs as ZIP, and the nested-EPUB rule silently imports the first work in the backup as a new standalone work titled after the backup file. Nothing is restored and no error is shown. This matches iOS's `nestedEPUB(in:)`, so it is parity, not a regression from iOS. It is still wrong behaviour that the brief's 'check how a .kudosbackup picked there is handled' should have surfaced rather than reported as handled.
confirmed.evidence: ArchiveWorkConverter.kt:27-30 `// 1. A nested EPUB wins outright … members.firstOrNull { (name, body) -> name.endsWith(".epub", ignoreCase = true) && ImportedFileFormat.sniff(body, name) == ImportedFileFormat.EPUB }?.let { return it.second }`; backup entries are `"$WORKS_DIRECTORY/${canonicalUuid(workId, "work.id")}.epub"` (BackupPaths.kt:78); 3ga-result.md: "A backup ZIP without readable work entries reports the archive-specific error".

verdict.why:
I confirmed this by reading the code. The patch changes the import picker to `*/*` (SettingsPages2.kt `EpubOpenMimeTypes`), so a .kudosbackup file reaches `WorkImporter.importLocalEpub`. One caveat: the old list already allowed application/octet-stream, which is likely what Android reports for that extension, so the picker change may not be the only way in.

How a real backup is handled:
1. `ImportedFileFormat.sniff` returns ZIP. The backup has no top-level `META-INF/container.xml`, and its name does not end in .epub.
2. `ArchiveWorkConverter.convert` (lines 27-30) returns the first member ending in `.epub` that sniffs as EPUB. Backup entries are `Works/<uuid>.epub` (BackupPaths.kt:26,78), and the name alone makes `sniff` return EPUB, so the first backed-up work is returned unchanged.
3. Back in `importLocalEpub`, `format` is ZIP, so `epubMetadata` is null and the `WorkIdentityIndex` duplicate check is skipped. The title is `titleFromDisplayName(displayName)` (e.g. "Kudos-<day>"), because `CalibreMetadata` won't parse binary ZIP bytes.

The result is one standalone work named after the backup file. Nothing is restored and no error is shown. iOS's `nestedEPUB(in:)` (ImportedDocumentConverter.swift:188) behaves the same way, so this matches iOS. The 'archive-specific error' only appears when no readable entries are found, which does not cover a normal backup with Works/*.epub entries.

confirmed.problem: When the submit lands back on AO3's login page with no flash error, Android still shows its own generic 'Login failed' message. iOS, in the same `.submitting` state, hands off to the visible AO3 page (`fallbackRequired`). That covers cases such as a CAPTCHA or interstitial, where showing AO3's own page is the only way forward. The brief's #12 asks to fall back 'as iOS does'.
confirmed.evidence: Android :311-314 `// Failed login landed back on login page. loading = false message = inspection.errorMessage ?: "Login failed. Check your username and password."`. iOS AO3WebLoginCoordinator.swift `case .submitting: if let message = observation.errorMessage { failHidden(.invalidCredentials(message)) } else { failHidden(.fallbackRequired(Self.fallbackPrompt)) }`.

verdict.why: I confirmed this by reading the code. In the patched AO3NativeLoginScreen.kt, onPageFinished first checks `loading && inspection.errorMessage != null`, which shows AO3's flash error. A page that is not the login page then just waits. The last branch (`!pendingSubmit && loading && url contains /users/login`, around lines 307-315) only runs when errorMessage is null. That makes the patch's `inspection.errorMessage ?:` dead code: this branch always shows the generic "Login failed. Check your username and password." text. It never sets `useWebFallback = true`, so the screen does not switch to AO3's visible page. iOS AO3WebLoginCoordinator.swift handles `case .submitting` with `if let message = observation.errorMessage { failHidden(.invalidCredentials(message)) } else { failHidden(.fallbackRequired(Self.fallbackPrompt)) }`. So when the submit lands back on the login page without an error (for example a CAPTCHA or interstitial), iOS hands off to AO3's page and Android shows a misleading credentials error and stays on its hidden WebView. The same patch already copied iOS's fallback for the fill failure (line ~281) and the timeout (line ~119), which makes this gap inconsistent with the brief's #12. The fix is small: in that branch, set `useWebFallback = true` and `message = FallbackPrompt`. A smaller gap: iOS also falls back on any other non-logged-in page it lands on, while Android waits for the 25s timeout, which then falls back anyway.

confirmed.problem: The Queue Storage author line switched from 12sp grey text to the shared work-detail byline, which draws at 15.5sp Medium in the accent colour. The byline is now larger than the row's 15sp title, which flips the row's hierarchy and makes rows taller. iOS uses a compact caption-size byline here. Under AGENTS.md's UI-consistency rule this is a density and visual regression.
confirmed.evidence: QueueStorageScreen.kt:242 `io.github.cidy02.kudos.works.detail.VerifiedAuthorByline(work.author, work.authorIdentitiesJSON)` (was `Text(work.author, color = tokens.secondaryInk, fontSize = 12.sp)`); title above it is `fontSize = 15.sp`; WorkDetailIdentity.kt AuthorBylineRow `fontSize = 15.5.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Medium`. iOS ReadingQueues.swift `AO3AuthorBylineView(… includesBy: false, font: .caption, compact: true)`.

verdict.why: The finding is confirmed. In the diff, QueueStorageScreen.kt:242 replaced `Text(work.author, color = tokens.secondaryInk, fontSize = 12.sp)` with `VerifiedAuthorByline(work.author, work.authorIdentitiesJSON)`. VerifiedAuthorByline has no size or style parameter. It always calls the private AuthorBylineRow in WorkDetailIdentity.kt, which draws every name at `fontSize = 15.5.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Medium` (accent colour when linked, otherwise secondaryInk) inside a FlowRow, and uses 15.5sp for the Anonymous fallback and the comma separators too. The title just above is 15.sp SemiBold, so the byline is now bigger than the title and the row gets taller. iOS is the source of truth, and ReadingQueues.swift preservedWorkRow (around line 383) uses a compact caption-size byline here: `AO3AuthorBylineView(displayText:, identities:, includesBy: false, font: .caption, compact: true)`, under a `.subheadline.weight(.semibold)` title. Android needs a compact or caption variant (around 12sp) to match, so as written this is a density and visual-hierarchy regression under the AGENTS.md UI-consistency rule.
